paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Following Jesus costs something, and He tells you so up front. He doesn't hide the price. Jesus resolutely sets out for Jerusalem (Luke 9:51), and anyone who walks with Him is walking behind Someone who already knows where the road goes.

Look at the three people who say they'll follow. One says, "I will follow You wherever You go." Jesus answers that the Son of Man "has no place to lay His head" (Luke 9:57-58). The other two say "first," and Jesus tells one to "go and proclaim the kingdom of God" (Luke 9:59-61). I think "first" is a very human word, friend. I've said it myself: "I'll get to it first thing, right after one more thing." Jesus isn't shaming anybody there. He's showing what following Him looks like when He comes first.

Then comes the plow. "No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God" (Luke 9:62). A plow only goes straight when your eyes are up ahead, and following Jesus works the same way. So here's your question, baker: what is your "first"? Hand it over to Him today, keep your eyes forward, and know that the One you're following is going to Jerusalem for you.
